sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-07-v15-quick/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 26 (#25) and Internal Quality Checks row 26 (#25, no internal annotation in E-Z)
npm pack @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 README.md (Core automation tools: browser_click modifiers, browser_run_code_unsafe)
evidence: All five dimension prompts open with 'Evaluate the live Colderwater playground at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP' (gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1, scored/visual/prompt.md:1), matching the template's opening line. Each judge.toml wires the playwright stdio MCP server (playwright-mcp --headless --isolated, chromium); functional adds the verifier restart server. Every prompt forbids source-based scoring: render 'Use only rendered browser behavior'; constraints 'decide it from the listed DOM facts only, not from file names, bundled library names or how the code looks'; functional:22 'do not read implementation files to infer success', :11 'A criterion passes only on evidence you gathered yourself in this session'; polish:19 'do not read implementation files', :11; visual:13 'Score from screenshots and the rendered page you observed yourself in this session', :20 'Do not read implementation files'. First-paint guesses are excluded: render criterion requires load plus reload; scored prompts require interaction (visual:14 type a ten-line draft, Run, click into code, watch caret 2s, double-click a word before screenshots); functional/polish require real key presses and clicks and quoted observations. {app_context} is substituted into every prompt by test.sh:198-200. New bullet app_context.md:21 ('A modifier-click means the modifier key is held down during the click. With the click tool, pass the modifier in its modifiers option; in the code runner, use page.keyboard.down ..., page.mouse.click ..., then page.keyboard.up') strengthens browser driving and is feasible on the pinned tool: @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 (tests/Dockerfile:19) README lists browser_click with 'modifiers (array, optional)' and browser_run_code_unsafe ('invoked with a single argument, page') under Core automation, i.e. enabled without --caps, consistent with the judge.toml args. It is consistent with app_context.md:20 (page.mouse/page.keyboard is real input, not a limited script use) and :29 (only three state-changing script uses), and with functional:22 which lists modifier-clicks as real interaction; it does not invite DOM dispatch or source reading. Frozen hashes of app_context.md (b8edd230...) and the four checked prompts match manifest.json. Counterexamples tried: (a) broken app whose source looks complete but serves a blank/dead workspace - every prompt's gate or criteria require live loading and interaction, so it cannot pass by source; a source-reading judge path is explicitly forbidden. (b) Conforming app whose Alt/Ctrl+Click works but judge's clicks lacked the modifier (the hosted Oracle failure) - now addressed by the new bullet; that failure itself shows the judge was driving the browser, not scoring from source. Not exercised: no full configured judge run on this exact candidate shows the judge now holds the modifier; that is outcome/tool-feasibility evidence for other rows, not for whether prompts drive the browser.
